title: Zerodha Enters Investment Banking After SEBI Grants Merchant Banking Licence
excerpt: India's largest discount broker will focus on equity IPOs for new-age businesses through its newly approved subsidiary, Zerodha Corporate Advisors.
body:
• SEBI has approved Zerodha Corporate Advisors for a Category-I merchant banking licence, with registration dated September 1
  • The wholly owned subsidiary will initially focus on equity IPOs, particularly for new-age businesses preparing to go public
  • Zerodha infused ₹55 crore into the subsidiary to meet SEBI's recently raised minimum net worth requirement of ₹50 crore
  • The move comes as Zerodha's core brokerage revenue declined to ₹2,738 crore in FY26 from ₹3,600 crore in FY24

Zerodha has received regulatory approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India to launch merchant banking operations, marking the discount brokerage giant's formal entry into investment banking.

Zerodha Corporate Advisors, a wholly owned subsidiary that applied for a Category-I merchant banking licence on April 27, received its registration from SEBI on September 1. The approval brings the total number of registered merchant bankers in India to 249.

"We've received the licence and will start operations over the next couple of months. We deliberately refrained from soliciting business before the licence was approved, and will build the mandate pipeline over the coming months."

— Mohit Mehra, Whole-time Director, Zerodha Corporate Advisors

IPO Market Entry

Zerodha Corporate Advisors will initially focus on equity capital markets, including initial public offerings, follow-on issues, and related advisory services. Mehra told Inc42 the firm plans to target "new-age businesses looking to raise capital from the public markets."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=HfnG9UiWKho

As a Category-I merchant banker, the subsidiary can manage main-board public issues, underwrite securities, and provide corporate finance and issue-related services. The licence also opens the door to activities such as mergers and acquisitions advisory and corporate restructuring.

The timing aligns with a rebound in India's primary market. IPO activity picked up sharply in July and August 2026, which together accounted for nearly 69 percent of IPO capital raised so far this year, according to Moneycontrol.

Diversification Push

Zerodha has housed the merchant banking business in a separate entity to maintain a clear separation from its broking operations and strengthen compliance safeguards. The Bengaluru-based company infused ₹55 crore into the subsidiary to meet SEBI's recently raised minimum net worth requirement, which jumped from ₹5 crore to ₹50 crore under revised regulations.

The expansion is part of a broader strategy to build revenue streams beyond Zerodha's core discount broking business, which has come under pressure from regulatory changes. The company reported revenue of ₹7,464 crore and profit after tax of ₹4,283 crore in FY26, but brokerage revenue declined to ₹2,738 crore from ₹3,066 crore in FY25 and ₹3,600 crore in FY24.

In recent years, Zerodha has diversified into mutual funds through its Coin platform, asset management, lending via Zerodha Capital, and startup investments through its Rainmatter arm. The company also holds a broker-dealer registration in GIFT City to facilitate overseas investments.

Competitive Landscape

Zerodha's entry intensifies competition in a market dominated by established investment banks including JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Axis Capital, and ICICI Securities. The company's large retail client base — built through its zero-brokerage model on delivery trades — could give it an advantage in marketing IPOs to individual investors, though institutional advisory mandates will require building an entirely new capability.

What to Watch

Zerodha Corporate Advisors expects to begin operations within two months, with the first IPO mandates likely to follow shortly after. For Indian investors and diaspora market watchers, the move signals that India's largest retail broker is betting heavily on the primary market as its next growth engine — a shift that could reshape how new-age companies access public capital.
